event_day_in_year.note: The day the rest of the model solves in full, located inside the year so its claim to be the hottest day is checkable rather than asserted.

provenance.source: ERA5 reanalysis via the Open-Meteo archive (free, no key)
provenance.grid_cell_note: ERA5's cell is about 0.25 deg (~25 km) and the one containing Midtown also contains open water and New Jersey. It is a regional 2 m air temperature, not an urban one, which is what the bias correction is for.
provenance.convention: hourly values are means over the preceding hour, local time

bias_correction.method: diurnal offset, cyclic linear interpolation over 8 anchors
bias_correction.amplitude_effect: ERA5's diurnal amplitude over this cell is 8.7 K wider than FortyGuard's urban field, so the correction is mostly an amplitude correction rather than a level shift.
bias_correction.limitation: The curve is fitted to a single day — the one day FortyGuard and ERA5 both cover — so it captures the shape of the bias but not its seasonality. A winter offset is an extrapolation. Both the corrected and the raw series are carried through to the web app, and every product derived from the corrected series is labelled 'reanalysis (bias-corrected)', never 'measured'.

sensitivity.definition: dT_surface / dT_air at 2 m, K/K, per facade panel and band
sensitivity.measured_by: re-solving the scene with the air-temperature anchor raised 1 K, at 16 hours spanning the year and the day
sensitivity.use: The browser paints a month's solved field plus gamma times the selected day's air-temperature departure from that month's representative day. Validated against a full re-solve in scripts/validate.py.

reconstruction.method: every day of the year solved at one hour and compared against its own month's reconstruction
reconstruction.reading: The residual is solar geometry, not weather. Two days a fortnight apart differ by several degrees of declination, which moves the shadow line and changes the incidence angle on every lit band, and no scalar applied to a solved field reproduces that. It is therefore largest in the equinox months, where declination moves fastest, and smallest in June and December where it barely moves. The twelve monthly days are solved rather than interpolated for exactly this reason; this is what remains between them.

shading_discrepancy.reading: The analytic canyon form and the ray-traced mask can only differ in the ground band, because that is the only band the raster vetoes. The difference is the obstruction a 2-D cross-section cannot see: corners, plazas, and the far side of an intersection. The annual tier uses the analytic form alone, so its sunlit-hour totals carry this over-estimate in the ground band and none above it.

tiers.event: 2 July 2026, 8 hours, every panel, ray-traced shadows, FortyGuard measured anchor. The validated tier.
tiers.month: 12 representative days, 8 hours each, every panel, ray-traced shadows, bias-corrected ERA5 anchor. The fields the browser paints.
tiers.annual: 8,760 hours, every panel, analytic canyon shading, accumulated not stored. Totals and extremes only.
tiers.day_within_month: month field + dT_surface/dT_air times the day's air-temperature departure, plus the surface-to-air excess scaled by the irradiance ratio on lit bands. Its error is MEASURED for every day against a full re-solve — see `reconstruction` — and the interface prints that day's own figure.
